## Threads

**Complexity as foundation cost.** The vault is a week old and runs 11 scripts, 5 LaunchAgents, a vector DB, and an MCP server. The tension with [[2026-03-11-amber-case-calm-technology]] and [[2026-03-11-school-for-poetic-computation]] is real but temporal — the complexity now is the cost of calm later. Nobody looks at wet concrete and calls it an un-calm building. As the system stabilizes and hands off into the chops suite (alongside tempor planning), the surface experience becomes lighter even as the substrate grows. The goal is high capture, self-organizing, bloom-generating — a system that's less visible but more present.

**Liveness is interactivity.** Not the weekly artifact alone (that's a document), but the moment of engaging with the mirror and having it respond. This reflect session was the first real experience of system liveness — provocations landed, pushback happened, new thinking emerged. The [[2026-03-12-governance-liveness-agentic-era]] assertion talks about liveness in DAO/agentic contexts, but the lived experience of liveness is here, in the vault's feedback loop. These are related but distinct — the governance talk is a pragmatic work deliverable; the vault's liveness is a personal practice.

**Plunge — a new feature concept.** A stochastic deep dive into vault history, weighted by: stale assertions, unanswered provocations, undeveloped ideas, dormant clusters, high-link-density notes gone cold. Not random — an archaeology of your own attention. Inspired by Apple Photos memories but for thinking, not brunch. Every plunge is a micro-reflect: "you wrote this 3 months ago — is it still true?" Feeds the Tamagotchi loop from the product vision. This would be a fifth temporal mode alongside real-time (inbox), periodic (daily/weekly), on-demand (reflect/signal), and now stochastic (plunge).

**Tool, not relationship.** Carefully framed: the system is a high-powered journal with a feedback loop. Not a digital friend, not Her, not a Kurzweilian singularity. You can appreciate a tool and enjoy a liminal personality in the interaction without it becoming a Black Mirror dependency. The calm technology ethic applies here — healthy relationship with technology means it's just that, or a little bit more. The product vision should never drift toward "build a digital companion." It's a reflective practice engine.

**Network effects of AI + existing vaults.** Obsidian and markdown vaults aren't new. Thousands of people have years of notes. The new puzzle piece is AI that can read the whole vault, find patterns, ask questions, generate synthesis. This isn't a new category of tech — it's a massive upgrade to an existing practice. Both from a productivity angle and from this more emotional/psychological/scientific inquiry angle. Not everything in the vault needs to be profound. Sometimes you clip something because you didn't have time and that's just it.

## New Thinking

- **Reflective practice engine** as the product frame — not assistant, not tool, not relationship. A system that makes you better at thinking by showing you your own patterns. Different from everything in the current landscape (Readwise, Notion AI, Mem0).
- **Five modes of engagement** for Layer 3: graph view (spatial), timeline scrub (temporal), plunge (stochastic), reflect (dialogue), signal (curated reading). Each surfaces different aspects of the same data.
- **The suite vision is emerging:** mind-palace (knowledge/memory) + chops (orchestration) + tempor (planning) as a composed but independent toolkit. Each standalone, together multiplicative.
- **The queue should serve you, not the other way around.** No guilt mechanics. Unconsumed items are fine. The system handles graceful neglect.

## Open Questions

- What does Layer 3 actually look like technically? Tauri + Svelte for the warm visual experience? How does the graph visualization work at scale?
- How does plunge work mechanically? Daily notification? Card in Obsidian? Slash command? All three?
- The governance assertion is the vault's strongest thread but the talk itself is a separate deliverable. When does that get structured beyond "I want to build a presentation"?
- What's the first thing a new user would experience if they installed this? The onboarding moment matters for whether the tool-not-relationship frame lands.
- Kat the poet engineer's digital garden — what specifically about that design feels right? Worth clipping concrete examples.
